source: Split each beat in two. Strum down on the number and up on the and: one and two and. That's eight strums per bar.

source: This traditional spiritual became a jazz standard. It uses C, D, E, F and G on strings 5, 4 and 3.

source: Travis picking, named after Merle Travis, keeps the thumb alternating on every beat while the fingers pluck in between, on the ands.
old: Mtindo wa Travis, uliopewa jina la Merle Travis, hufanya gumba lipokezane kwenye kila pigo huku vidole vikipiga katikati, kwenye na.
new: Katika mtindo wa Travis, uliopewa jina la Merle Travis, gumba hupiga nyuzi za besi kwa kupokezana kwenye kila pigo huku vidole vingine vikipiga katikati, kwenye na.
reason: A single thumb does not reciprocally take turns with itself. State that it plays alternating bass strings; the adjacent lesson establishes these strings. Retain named technique and offbeat contrast.

source: Alternates bass notes on every beat

new: Hupiga noti za besi kwa kupokezana kila pigo

source: Lifting straight up lets the note die. A small sideways flick plucks the lower note into life.
old: Kuinua moja kwa moja hukatisha sauti. Kuvuta kidole kidogo pembeni huifanya noti ya chini ilie.
new: Kuinua moja kwa moja hukatisha sauti. Kuvuta kidole pembeni kidogo huifanya noti ya chini ilie.
reason: Old kidole kidogo means little finger, whereas source calls for a small sideways flick of the active finger. Attach kidogo to the lateral movement, not to kidole.

source: Sixteenth notes split each beat in four: one-e-and-a, two-e-and-a. Your strumming hand doubles its speed, down-up-down-up inside every beat.
old: Noti za kumi na sita hugawa kila pigo mara nne: moja-e-na-a, mbili-e-na-a. Mkono wa kupiga huwa na kasi maradufu, chini-juu-chini-juu ndani ya kila pigo.
new: Noti za kumi na sita hugawa kila pigo katika sehemu nne: moja-e-na-a, mbili-e-na-a. Mkono wa kupiga huwa na kasi maradufu, chini-juu-chini-juu ndani ya kila pigo.
reason: mara nne means four times rather than into four equal rhythmic subdivisions; use sehemu nne.

source: Alternate the bass

new: Piga noti za besi kwa kupokezana
reason: The imperative Pokezana besi incorrectly applies a reciprocal verb directly to bass. Specify playing alternating bass notes, supported by the string-switching body.

source: Most songs alternate two sections. The verse tells the story; the chorus repeats the hook. Stephen Foster's Oh! Susanna (1848) has both. Capo off: it's in G.
old: Nyimbo nyingi hupokezana sehemu mbili. Ubeti husimulia; kiitikio hurudia kishazi cha kuvutia. Oh! Susanna ya Stephen Foster (1848) ina zote mbili. Ondoa kapo: iko katika G.
new: Nyimbo nyingi huwa na sehemu mbili zinazopokezana. Ubeti husimulia; kiitikio hurudia kishazi cha kuvutia. Oh! Susanna ya Stephen Foster (1848) ina zote mbili. Ondoa kapo: iko katika G.
reason: Sections alternate within a song; songs do not take turns with sections. Restore the subject/object relationship while preserving form, name/year and key.

source: Timbre accepts a note within 30 cents, about a third of a half step. If you're sharp, nudge the finger toward the scroll. If you're flat, nudge it toward the bridge.

new: Timbre hukubali noti iliyo ndani ya senti 30, karibu theluthi ya nusu toni. Sauti ikiwa juu mno, sogeza kidole kuelekea kichwani kwa kiasi kidogo. Ikiwa chini mno, kisogeze kuelekea daraja la nyuzi kwa kiasi kidogo.

source: Fret a note, pick it, then pull your finger slightly sideways as you lift. That flick plucks the open string, so a second note sounds without the pick.

source: B to C sharp is a whole step, so 1 and 2 have a gap. C sharp to D is a half step, so 2 and 3 touch.

source: This song rocks in six-eight: two big beats a bar, each split in three. Count one-two-three, four-five-six, like oars pulling and coming back.
old: Wimbo huu huyumba kwa sita kwa nane: mapigo mawili makubwa kwa kipimo, kila moja likigawanywa mara tatu. Hesabu moja-mbili-tatu, nne-tano-sita, kama makasia yanayovutwa na kurudishwa.
new: Wimbo huu huyumba kwa sita kwa nane: mapigo mawili makubwa kwa kipimo, kila moja likigawanywa katika sehemu tatu. Hesabu moja-mbili-tatu, nne-tano-sita, kama makasia yanayovutwa na kurudishwa.
reason: 6/8 compound beats divide into three parts, not three repeated divisions.

source: The beat is the steady pulse you tap your foot to. It never rushes or drags, like footsteps on an easy walk. Every rhythm sits on top of it.
old: Pigo ni mwendo thabiti unaoufuata kwa kugonga mguu. Haliharakishi wala kuchelewa, kama hatua za kutembea kwa utulivu. Kila mdundo hujengwa juu yake.
new: Pigo ni mwendo thabiti unaoufuata kwa kugonga mguu. Haliharakishi wala halichelewi, kama hatua za kutembea kwa utulivu. Kila mdundo hujengwa juu yake.
reason: Parallel negative finite predicates for the steady pulse.

source: Faster tempos need less effort, not more. Keep your hand loose and tap from the knuckle, not the wrist or shoulder.
old: Tempo za haraka huhitaji juhudi kidogo zaidi, si nyingi zaidi. Mkono ubaki umelegea, ugonge kwa kusogeza kifundo cha kidole, si cha mkono wala bega.
new: Tempo za haraka huhitaji juhudi chache zaidi, si nyingi zaidi. Mkono ubaki umelegea, ugonge kwa kusogeza kifundo cha kidole, si cha mkono wala bega.
reason: Use matching class-10 quantification for juhudi while clearly expressing less effort.

source: Hover just above the glass between taps. A short, light motion is easier to keep even at faster tempos.
old: Kaa juu kidogo tu ya kioo kati ya miguso. Mwendo mfupi mwepesi ni rahisi kudumisha kwa usawa katika tempo za haraka zaidi.
new: Weka ncha ya kidole juu kidogo tu ya kioo kati ya miguso. Mwendo mfupi mwepesi ni rahisi kudumisha kwa usawa katika tempo za haraka zaidi.
reason: The fingertip hovers above the glass, not the learner sitting/staying above it; make the physical referent explicit.

source: Your note wobbles and fades. What helps most?
old: Noti yako inayumba na kupungua sauti. Nini husaidia zaidi?
new: Noti yako inayumba na sauti yake inapungua. Nini husaidia zaidi?
reason: Use parallel finite clauses and make fading loudness explicit.

source: Clear your throat hard
old: Koholewa kwa nguvu kusafisha koo
new: Kohoa kwa nguvu kusafisha koo
reason: Correct the imperative to kohoa; koholewa is a passive form. This remains the intentionally wrong distractor, not a recommendation.

source: Stop, rest, and try it softer
old: Simama, pumzika, ujaribu kwa sauti ndogo
new: Acha kuimba, pumzika, ujaribu kwa sauti ndogo
reason: Stop here means cease singing, not stand up; retain the safe rest-and-softer retry instruction.

source: A note feels tight or scratchy. What do you do?
old: Noti inahisi imebana au inakwaruza. Ufanye nini?
new: Unahisi kubana au kukwaruza unapoimba noti. Ufanye nini?
reason: The singer experiences tightness/scratchiness; avoid saying the note itself feels.

source: A regular wave in pitch
old: Wimbi la kawaida katika kimo cha sauti
new: Wimbi la kimo cha sauti linalojirudia kwa usawa
reason: Regular vibrato means an evenly recurring pitch wave, not an ordinary/kawaida wave. Matches corrected vibrato definition.

source: E to F has no note between them. C to D and G to A are whole steps.
old: E hadi F hazina noti katikati yake. C hadi D na G hadi A ni toni nzima.
new: Hakuna noti kati ya E na F. C hadi D na G hadi A ni toni nzima.
reason: Explicit note-pair wording naturally expresses no intervening note; avoids plural verb with a span phrase.

source: Between which two steps is there a half step?
old: Ni hatua zipi mbili zina nusu toni katikati yake?
new: Ni hatua zipi mbili zimetengana kwa nusu toni?
reason: The two steps are a half step apart; express the interval directly and preserve the Mi-to-fa correct answer.

source: This American hymn tune from the early 1800s is in 3/4: count 1, 2, 3. Long notes often turn into a quick pair, so keep the pair light.
old: Melodi hii ya tenzi ya Marekani ya mwanzoni mwa karne iliyoanza 1800 iko katika 3/4: hesabu 1, 2, 3. Noti ndefu mara nyingi hugeuka jozi ya haraka, hivyo jozi ibaki nyepesi.
new: Melodi hii ya wimbo wa dini wa Marekani ya mwanzoni mwa karne iliyoanza 1800 iko katika 3/4: hesabu 1, 2, 3. Noti ndefu mara nyingi hugeuka jozi ya haraka, hivyo jozi ibaki nyepesi.
reason: One American hymn tune, not a plural collection of hymns; consistent with related hymn prompts.

source: Notes often sag flat as your air runs out. Stop a little before you're empty, then take a fresh low breath.
old: Noti mara nyingi hushuka chini ya kimo sahihi hewa inapokwisha. Simama kidogo kabla haijaisha, kisha vuta pumzi mpya tumboni.
new: Noti mara nyingi hushuka chini ya kimo sahihi hewa inapokwisha. Maliza noti muda mfupi kabla hewa haijaisha, kisha vuta pumzi mpya tumboni.
reason: Stop short means finish the sung note before the breath runs out, not stand briefly.

source: A swell grows from soft to louder and back on one breath. Start quietly, grow gently, then fade, all on the same pitch.
old: Sauti huongezeka kutoka ndogo hadi kubwa zaidi, kisha kurudi, kwa pumzi moja. Anza kimya, ongeza kwa upole, kisha punguza, yote katika kimo kilekile.
new: Sauti huongezeka kutoka ndogo hadi kubwa zaidi, kisha kurudi, kwa pumzi moja. Anza kwa sauti ndogo, ongeza kwa upole, kisha punguza, yote katika kimo kilekile.
reason: Begin quietly means sing softly, not begin in silence; preserve sustained same-pitch swell.

reason: March is the musical march, not a protest demonstration; matches reviewed comparison explanation.

source: Rock between open E and D sharp at fret 4 on string 2, then walk down B, D, C to A.

new: Piga E wazi na D diesi kwenye freti 4 ya uzi 2 kwa kupokezana, kisha shuka B, D, C hadi A.

source: Most of the tune runs in eighth notes. Keep the pick small and alternate down and up, so you never fall behind.
